blocks.text: ONE OF THE LORD'S BROTHERS (MARK 6:3)
Jude, the Lord's brother. A name in the family list at Nazareth; Hegesippus tells of his grandsons brought before an emperor.
ALSO CALLED
Juda (Mark 6:3) · Judas (Matthew 13:55)
FROM
He is named among the family the people of Jesus' “own country” knew (Mark 6:1-3).
TRADE
Scripture does not say
FAMILY
He is one of the four brothers the people at Nazareth name: “James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon”.
WRITINGS
The letter of Jude (who wrote it is a question on the Letters page)
BACKGROUND
Home, trade and family
FROM
FAMILY
He is one of the four brothers the people at Nazareth name: “James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon”. Mark 6:3 Matthew 13:55
From the textMark spells the name “Juda”, Matthew “Judas”; the Greek is the same name, which the letter of Jude also uses. Mark 6:3 Matthew 13:55 Jude 1:1
Paul says “the brethren of the Lord” had the right “to lead about a sister, a wife”, as the other apostles did; he does not say which brothers. 1 Corinthians 9:5

Early church · Eusebius (trans. A. C. McGiffert, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, series 2, vol. 1), 1890Hegesippus (about AD 170) knew of grandsons of “Jude, who is said to have been the Lord's brother according to the flesh”.[1]
WITH JESUS
His moments with Jesus
WHERE HE WENT
Acts and after
Nazareth · Jesus' “own country” (Mark 6:1), where the people named his brothers; Mark names Nazareth as the town Jesus came from (Mark 1:9). Mark 1:9 Mark 6:1–3
Jerusalem · With the other brothers in the upper room after the ascension. Acts 1:12–14
IN ACTS AND THE LETTERS
After the ascension the Lord's brothers pray with the apostles, the women and Mary the mother of Jesus. Acts 1:14
Paul names “the brethren of the Lord” with the other apostles and Cephas as having the right “to lead about a sister, a wife”. 1 Corinthians 9:5

From the textScripture names this Jude only in the two Nazareth lists (Mark 6:3; Matthew 13:55). Acts 1:14 and 1 Corinthians 9:5 speak of the brothers as a group. Mark 6:3 Matthew 13:55 Acts 1:14 1 Corinthians 9:5
COMPANIONS
Who was with him
Each line joins him to someone Scripture places beside him.
James, the Lord's brother Named first of the brothers, with Jude. Mark 6:3 Matthew 13:55
Mary the mother of Jesus Named with the brothers in the upper room. Acts 1:14
Simon, one of the brothers Named with him among the brothers. Mark 6:3
Joses, one of the brothers Named with him among the brothers. Mark 6:3
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
From the textScripture names Jude only in the Nazareth lists; after that the brothers appear only as a group (Acts 1:14). It records nothing of his death. Acts 1:14
TRADITION SAYS

“Of the family of the Lord there were still living the grandchildren of Jude, who is said to have been the Lord's brother according to the flesh.” Accused of being of David's line, they were brought before the emperor Domitian; they owned only “a piece of land which contained only thirty-nine acres”, and supported themselves by their own labour.[1] Who says so: Hegesippus, quoted by Eusebius, Church History 3.19-20, Hegesippus about AD 170; Domitian reigned 81-96

Eusebius adds, in his own words, that they showed their work-hardened hands, said Christ's kingdom was “not a temporal nor an earthly kingdom, but a heavenly and angelic one”, and were let go. McGiffert notes that the quotation from Hegesippus ends before this part.[1][2] Who says so: Eusebius, Church History 3.20.5-7, about AD 325

“They came, therefore, and took the lead of every church as witnesses and as relatives of the Lord”, and lived until the reign of Trajan.[1] Who says so: Hegesippus, quoted by Eusebius, Church History 3.32.5-6, Hegesippus about AD 170; Trajan reigned 98-117

Writers who took this Jude to be the apostle Thaddaeus gave him that apostle's story. The Golden Legend calls the apostle Judas “brother to James the Less” and has him and Simon cut down in Persia.[26] Who says so: Jacobus de Voragine, The Golden Legend (Caxton's English, ed. Ellis 1900), about 1260

Writings tied to him

OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
Two different men
A. C. McGiffert (1890); J. B. Lightfoot (1890), who notes that the writer of Jude “seems to disclaim for himself the title of an Apostle”

The brothers did not believe in Jesus after the Twelve were chosen (John 7:5), and Acts 1:13-14 names the apostles and then, separately, “his brethren”. Luke's “Judas of James” is, McGiffert argues, the son of a James, not his brother. John 7:5 Acts 1:13–14 Luke 6:16 Jude 1:17 [2][13]
The same man

M. G. Easton (1897, under “Jude”), who lists Matthew 13:55 among the apostle's verses; the Golden Legend (about 1260); it follows from the cousin view, which counts the Lord's brothers among the Twelve, as H. E. Jacobs (ISBE, 1915) describes that view in full

Read with the KJV as “Judas the brother of James” (Luke 6:16; Acts 1:13), the apostle matches the Jude who calls himself “brother of James” (Jude 1) and the Judas named among the Lord's brothers (Matthew 13:55). Luke 6:16 Acts 1:13 Jude 1:1 Matthew 13:55 [15][26][23]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 8
Mark 6 Matthew 13 Mark 3 John 2 John 7 Acts 1 1 Corinthians 9 Jude 1
PASSAGES · 8
Mark 6:1–6 Matthew 13:54–58 Mark 3:31–35 John 2:12 John 7:2–10 Acts 1:14 1 Corinthians 9:5 Jude 1:1
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture records nothing Jude said or did as a person; he is a name in the Nazareth list and one of “his brethren”.
Scripture does not say how he was related to Joseph and Mary (see the question below), whether he travelled, or how he died.
Scripture does not say that he wrote the letter of Jude.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textThis page is about the brother named at Nazareth (Mark 6:3). Two other men called Judas appear among the first disciples: Judas Iscariot, and the apostle “Judas the brother of James” (Luke 6:16), where “the brother” is a word the KJV supplies. Mark 6:3 Luke 6:16

From the textThe letter of Jude opens “Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James”. It does not call its writer the Lord's brother, and it speaks of “the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ” as others (verse 17). Who wrote it is a question for the Letters page. Jude 1:1 Jude 1:17

Early church · Origen (trans. John Patrick, Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 9, ed. Allan Menzies), 1896Origen (about AD 245 or later) reads the letter's opening as the words of this Jude, the brother of James and of the Lord. Jude 1:1 [5]
